summary: The paper proves the first general results on cyclic base change functoriality in the Langlands correspondence over function fields, with mod p coefficients and without any trace formula. Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), with φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG the diagonal on dual groups. Theorem 1.1: every irreducible k-representation of H(F_v) has a base change to G(F_v), for the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimplified local Langlands correspondence. Theorem 1.2, the Treumann–Venkatesh conjecture: if Π is σ-fixed and π is an irreducible subquotient of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π) as an H(F_v)-representation, then φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^{(p)}} — Tate cohomology realises functoriality. Theorem 1.4: there is a base change homomorphism Z_TV of mod p Bernstein centers with the right effect on parameters, the construction Haines envisaged, for general groups and arbitrary depth. Theorem 1.6: strong global base change, transporting a whole automorphic L-parameter and not only the unramified Hecke eigensystem. The method has three layers. Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory is extended from finite type to locally finite type schemes, giving the Tate categories and the Smith operation Psm with its equivariant localisation theorem. Parity sheaves and Leslie–Lonergan's Tate-parity sheaves make the construction compatible with Geometric Satake, producing a base change functor BC on normalized parity sheaves which, by Theorem 4.20 and the appendix with Gus Lonergan, is restriction along the diagonal on tilting modules for the dual group: a categorification of the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh. Applied to moduli of shtukas, where Sht_H is the σ-fixed locus of Sht_G, this yields an identity between excursion operators for G and for H on Tate cohomology, and hence the global theorem; local-global compatibility of the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence then gives the local ones. What the atlas lacks: sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, Tate categories, parity sheaves, Tate-parity sheaves and tilting modules for a dual group in characteristic p; Tate cohomology of shtukas, Drinfeld's lemma for it, and the whole mod p side of Lafforgue's construction, the atlas's shtuka roadmap being written for ℓ-adic characteristic-zero coefficients; and mod p Bernstein centers at Moy–Prasad level with the Brauer homomorphism and the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence. What it already has: the excursion algebra with its relations and the reconstruction of semisimple L-parameters, shtuka stacks with legs and level, the dual group and the L-group, buildings and parahorics, and, in the libraries, Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group and Witt vectors.

items.name: Coefficients, σ-actions and the norm element
items.statement: k is an algebraic closure of F_p with the discrete topology; σ denotes a chosen generator of a group isomorphic to Z/pZ; N = 1 + σ + ··· + σ^{p-1} ∈ Z[σ] and also the induced operator on any Z[σ]-module, while Nm(a) = a * σ(a) * ··· * σ^{p-1}(a) in any monoidal setting. Geometric objects live over fields of characteristic ℓ ≠ p while the coefficients have characteristic p.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §1.6
items.note: This inversion of the usual arithmetic-geometry convention is the standing convention of Smith theory and is used throughout the paper.

items.name: Odd good primes for the dual group
items.statement: p is an odd good prime for G-hat if p > 2 when G-hat has simple factors of type A, B, C or D; p > 3 when it has simple factors of type G_2, F_4, E_6 or E_7; and p > 5 when it has simple factors of type E_8.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.2; the footnote to the hypothesis
items.note: The standing hypothesis of Theorems 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 and 6.26. Goodness of p is what makes all parity sheaves on Gr_G exist and be perverse (Theorem 4.8).

items.name: Existence of local mod p cyclic base change (Theorem 1.1)
items.statement: Let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}); let φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG be the admissible homomorphism which is the diagonal on the dual groups. Then for every irreducible representation π of H(F_v) over k there is an irreducible representation Π of G(F_v) over k with ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π, where ρ denotes the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimple L-parameter.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.1; proved as Theorem 6.26, which adds the hypothesis that p is an odd good prime for G-hat and the level control
items.note: The first general existence theorem for local cyclic base change of all irreducible representations of an arbitrary reductive group over a local function field, with no trace formula. Vignéras's full local Langlands gives a sharper statement for GL_n only.

items.name: Tate cohomology realises cyclic base change (Theorem 1.2)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let Π be an irreducible representation of G(F_v) over k whose isomorphism class is fixed by σ, with Π^{(p)} = Π ⊗_{k,Frob} k its Frobenius twist. Let π be any irreducible admissible subquotient of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π) as an H(F_v)-representation, with Genestier–Lafforgue parameter ρ_π: W_v → ^LH(k). Then φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^{(p)}}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.2; proved as Theorem 6.21
items.note: This verifies Conjecture 6.3 of Treumann–Venkatesh for the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence, uniformly in the group and the representation. It was known only for certain depth-zero supercuspidals of GL_n, by Ronchetti's direct computation.

items.name: Base change homomorphism for Bernstein centers (Theorem 1.4)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Then there is a homomorphism Z_TV: Z(G) → Z(H) of Bernstein centers with k-coefficients such that for every irreducible H(F_v)-representation π, and every irreducible G(F_v)-representation Π on which Z(G) acts through χ_π ∘ Z_TV, one has ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.4; constructed in Definition 6.11, its property proved in §6.3
items.note: A base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers in characteristic zero was sought by Haines and constructed in low depth; this is the first construction for general groups and depth, and the first with a proved relation to the local Langlands correspondence.

items.name: Existence of global mod p cyclic base change (Theorem 1.6)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let F be a global function field of characteristic ≠ p, H a reductive group over F, E/F cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E/F}(H_E). If ρ: Gal(F^s/F) → ^LH(k) is automorphic, i.e. arises from Lafforgue–Xue's excursion action on compactly supported automorphic functions, then φ_BC ∘ ρ is automorphic.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.6; proved as Theorem 5.13
items.note: This is strong base change: it concerns the whole L-parameter, not only the Hecke eigensystem at almost all places. The two notions coincide for GL_n but not for general groups — Lafforgue's correspondence can assign different parameters to automorphic forms generating isomorphic representations, already for SL_n with n ≥ 3.

items.name: The algebraic L-group
items.statement: For G reductive over a field F with separable closure F^s, the root datum Ψ(G) of G_{F^s} determines a pinning of the split reductive group G-hat over k, hence a splitting Out(G-hat) → Aut(G-hat) and an identification Aut(Ψ(G)) ≅ Out(G-hat); transporting the Gal(F^s/F)-action on Ψ(G) gives act^alg and ^LG^alg := G-hat ⋊_{act^alg} Gal(F^s/F), a pro-algebraic group over k since the action factors through a finite quotient. Over a local field the Weil form G-hat ⋊ Weil(F^s/F) is used instead.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.1.1
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 plans the pinned split dual group from the dual root datum together with the continuous finite-image action on its pinning and the semidirect L-group with its projection and action law.

items.name: The geometric L-group
items.statement: The Geometric Satake equivalence Perv_{L^+G_{F^s}}(Gr_{G,F^s};k) ≅ Rep_k(G-hat) carries the Gal(F^s/F)-action on Gr_{G,F^s} to an action act^geom on G-hat_k, and ^LG^geom := G-hat_k ⋊_{act^geom} Gal(F^s/F). The category Rep_k(^LG^geom) is the continuously Gal(F^s/F)-equivariant objects of Rep_k(G-hat) for act^geom, and descent gives Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Rep_k(G-hat)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.1.2; and §2.1.4
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4 plans Tannakian reconstruction of the dual group from the Satake category together with the Weil action, and GS4:integral-dual-group the normalized functoriality; this is that construction in the equal-characteristic setting with k-coefficients.

items.name: Comparison of the algebraic and geometric L-groups (Proposition 2.1)
items.statement: Let ρ be the half sum of the positive coroots of G-hat, viewed as a cocharacter G_m → G-hat_ad, cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → F_p^× the mod p cyclotomic character and χ = ρ ∘ cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → G-hat_ad(k). Then act^geom = act^alg ∘ Ad_χ. Consequently a lift χ-tilde of χ to G-hat(k), for instance from a square root of the cyclotomic character, gives an isomorphism ^LG^alg ≅ ^LG^geom by (g,γ) ↦ (g χ-tilde(γ^{-1}), γ); such a square root exists whenever char F > 0.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 2.1
items.note: The ρ-shift between the L-algebraic and C-algebraic normalisations. In general the two L-groups need not be isomorphic, but over a function field they are.

items.name: L-parameters and semisimplicity
items.statement: For Γ a topological group with a quotient Γ-bar acting on G-hat, an L-parameter from Γ to G-hat(k) ⋊ Γ-bar is a G-hat(k)-conjugacy class of continuous homomorphisms ρ: Γ → G-hat(k) ⋊ Γ-bar lying over the given quotient; equivalently an element of H^1_cts(Γ, G-hat(k)). ρ is semisimple (completely reducible) if whenever it factors through a parabolic ^LP^alg(k) it factors through a Levi ^LM^alg(k) of it.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.2
items.note: GS.5 plans the reconstruction of continuous semisimple L-group parameters, including the projection to the Galois group and the conjugacy convention for nonsplit G; ES0 plans the same in the local setting.

items.name: The excursion algebra, first presentation
items.statement: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) is the commutative k-algebra generated by symbols S_{I,f,(γ_i)} for I a finite set, f ∈ O(G-hat_k \ (^LG^alg_k)^I / G-hat_k) and γ_i ∈ Γ, subject to: S_{∅,f,*} = f(1); f ↦ S_{I,f,(γ_i)} is a k-algebra homomorphism; S_{J,f^ζ,(γ_j)} = S_{I,f,(γ_{ζ(i)})} for ζ: I → J; the triple relation S_{I⊔I⊔I, f-tilde, (γ)×(γ')×(γ'')} = S_{I,f,(γ_i(γ'_i)^{-1}γ''_i)}; and the inflation relation reducing a function pulled back from Γ^{I\J} to the index set J.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.3; with the generators of §2.2.1 and the relations of §2.2.2
items.note: GS.5 plans excursion operators indexed by invariant functions and Galois tuples with their relations and commutativity; ES0 plans the same construction from a finite leg set, an invariant function, creation, the Weil tuple and annihilation, with linearity, multiplication, reindexing, unit insertion and composition relations.

items.name: Langlands parameters from characters of the excursion algebra (Proposition 2.4)
items.statement: For any character ν: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → k there is a semisimple L-parameter ρ_ν: Γ → ^LG^alg(k) for the discrete topology on Γ, unique up to G-hat(k)-conjugacy, characterised by ν(S_{{0,...,n}, f, (γ_0,...,γ_n)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ_0γ_n), ..., ρ_ν(γ_{n-1}γ_n), ρ_ν(γ_n)) for all n, all invariant f and all tuples.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 2.4
items.note: Quoted from Lafforgue §13 and Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne Theorem 4.5. GS.5 plans exactly this reconstruction of semisimple parameters from characters of the excursion algebra.

items.name: The excursion algebra, second presentation
items.statement: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) is presented by generators S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} with W ∈ Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I), x ∈ W and ξ ∈ W^* invariant under the diagonal G-hat_k, subject to six families of relations: the empty-set evaluation, functoriality along morphisms of representations, multiplicativity for ☒ and additivity for ⊕ with k-linearity in x and ξ, restriction along ζ: I → J, the coevaluation/evaluation relation encoding γ(γ')^{-1}γ'', and inflation from a subset J. The two presentations agree via S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I,f_{x,ξ},(γ_i)} with f_{x,ξ}((g_i)) = ⟨ξ, (g_i)·x⟩.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.4; generators in §2.4.1, relations in §2.4.2, comparison in §2.4.3
items.note: This is the presentation ES0 describes (creation by a coevaluation map, a tuple of Weil elements, annihilation by evaluation, independence of the representation realising the function, by the parameter algebra's presentation), and the one GS.5 needs to construct actions.

items.name: Admissible homomorphisms of L-groups
items.statement: A homomorphism φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg is admissible if it lies over the identity of Γ.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.5
items.note: RG2.5 plans the L-group with its projection to the Galois group, of which admissibility is the compatibility condition.

items.name: Functoriality for excursion algebras (Lemma 2.7)
items.statement: For φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg admissible there is a homomorphism φ^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg), given on generators by S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} ↦ S_{I,Res_φ V, Res_φ x, Res_φ ξ, (γ_i)}, which on k-points of the corresponding spectra sends ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, H-hat(k)) to φ ∘ ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, G-hat(k)).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 2.7
items.note: This is Langlands functoriality translated into the excursion algebra; it is what makes the whole strategy of the paper possible. No layer of the atlas plans functoriality of the excursion algebra along an L-homomorphism.

items.name: The base change homomorphism of L-groups φ_BC
items.statement: For H reductive over F and G = Res_{E/F}(H_E) with E/F cyclic of degree p, φ_BC: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg is (h,γ) ↦ (Δ(h),γ) with Δ the diagonal H-hat → H-hat^p = G-hat; the same formula defines φ_BC^geom, and the two are compatible with the comparison isomorphism provided the same square root of the cyclotomic character is used for H and for G. φ_BC^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg) is the induced map.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.8
items.note: The compatibility of φ_BC with both normalisations of the L-group is what lets the geometric argument (which produces the geometric L-group) be read as a statement about the algebraic one.

items.name: Flat and perfect complexes over the group ring
items.statement: For Y a separated locally finite type scheme over a field and Λ a p-adic coefficient ring, Perf(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) is the full subcategory of complexes with perfect stalks, and Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) the full subcategory of bounded complexes whose stalks at geometric points are represented by bounded complexes of flat, not necessarily finite, Λ[σ]-modules.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 3.1
items.note: The enlargement from Perf to Flat^b is what makes the theory work for locally finite type schemes such as moduli of shtukas; see Remark 3.10.

items.name: Flat^b is finite tor-amplitude (Lemma 3.2)
items.statement: Flat^b(Y;k[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;k[σ]) coincides with the full subcategory of objects which locally have finite tor-amplitude over k[σ].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.2
items.note: Proved using that k[σ] is Artinian, so flat equals projective and the finitistic dimension is zero, whence a complex concentrated in degrees [a,b] with finite tor-amplitude has tor-amplitude in [a,b]. Not used essentially, but it identifies the subcategory.

items.name: The constructible and ind-constructible Tate categories
items.statement: The constructible Tate category of Y is the Verdier quotient D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ])/Perf(Y;Λ[σ]), written Perf(Y;T_Λ); the bounded ind-constructible Tate category is Shv(Y;T_Λ) := D^b(Y;Λ[σ])/Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]). The projections are both written T^*, and the induced functor Perf(Y;T_Λ) → Shv(Y;T_Λ) is conservative.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 3.3
items.note: Treumann's Tate category, extended from finite type to locally finite type. Nothing in the atlas plans Verdier quotients of equivariant derived categories by perfect or flat complexes.

items.name: The shift-by-2 functor is the identity on the Tate category (Example 3.4)
items.statement: On the Tate category over a point — the spectrum of a separably closed field — which is D^b(Λ[σ])/Flat^b(Λ[σ]), the shift-by-2 functor is isomorphic to the identity functor, as the nullhomotopic complex 0 → V → V⊗Λ[σ] →(1-σ) V⊗Λ[σ] → V → 0 has its middle two terms projecting to 0.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Example 3.4
items.note: This is why perverse sheaves cannot be seen in the Tate category and parity sheaves must replace them; it is the conceptual pivot of §4.

items.name: The Smith operation
items.statement: For Y a separated locally finite type scheme with an admissible σ-action, i: Y^σ ↪ Y the fixed locus and the identification D^b_σ(Y^σ;Λ) ≅ D^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]), the Smith operation is Psm := T^* ∘ i^*, defined both as D^b_{c,σ}(Y;Λ) → Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ) and as D^b_σ(Y;Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ); the two are compatible under Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.2; equations (3.3) and (3.4)
items.note: Treumann's functor, in the locally finite type generality the paper needs. Admissibility of the action is automatic when Y is exhausted by quasi-projective schemes over a field.

items.name: Pushforward along a free quotient is flat (Lemma 3.6)
items.statement: If the σ-action on Y is free with quotient q: Y → Y/σ, then q_* F ∈ Flat^b(Y/σ;Λ[σ]) for every F ∈ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.6
items.note: The stalk of q_*F at a geometric point is F_x-bar ⊗_Λ Λ[σ], visibly flat over Λ[σ].

items.name: Nearby stalks along the fixed locus are flat (Lemma 3.7)
items.statement: Let U := Y \ Y^σ with open immersion j. Then for any F ∈ D^b(U;Λ[σ]) and any geometric point y-bar of Y^σ, the stalk (Rj_* F)_{y-bar} lies in Flat^b(y-bar;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.7
items.note: Proved by total ramification of q at y-bar and the preservation of finite tor-amplitude by Rj-bar_*.

items.name: i^! and i^* agree in the Tate category (Lemma 3.8)
items.statement: For i: Y^σ ↪ Y and any F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;Λ), the cone of i^! F → i^* F belongs to Flat^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.8
items.note: This is the source of the good behaviour of Psm: in the Tate category the two restriction functors are identified. Proved for finite type schemes by Riche–Williamson, following Treumann in topology.

items.name: Proper pushforward preserves Flat^b (Lemma 3.9)
items.statement: If f: Y → S is a locally finite type separated σ-equivariant morphism of locally finite type schemes of bounded dimension, then Rf_!: D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) → D^b(S;Λ[σ]) carries Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]) into Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.9; with Remark 3.10
items.note: Remark 3.10 records that the statement is false with Flat^b replaced by Perf, which is exactly why the ind-constructible Tate category is needed outside the finite type situation.

items.name: Pushforward from a free action lands in Flat^b (Corollary 3.11)
items.statement: If in addition σ acts trivially on S and freely on Y, then Rf_!: D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) → D^b(S;Λ[σ]) lands in Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 3.11
items.note: Factor f through Y/σ and combine Lemmas 3.6 and 3.9. This is the vanishing that makes equivariant localisation work.

items.name: The six operations on Tate categories
items.statement: For f: Y → S σ-equivariant, locally finite type, of bounded dimension: f^* descends to Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) and to the constructible Tate categories since it preserves stalks; Rf_! descends by Lemma 3.9; and on the constructible Tate categories Verdier duality D descends, so f^! := D f^* D and Rf_* := D f_! D are defined. The Smith operation commutes with f^*, f^!, Rf_* and Rf_!.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.3; and Appendix A §A.1
items.note: The slogan is that the Smith operation commutes with all operations; the compatibility with Rf_* follows from that with Rf_! by duality and Lemma 3.8.

items.name: The Smith operation commutes with proper pushforward (Proposition 3.12)
items.statement: For f: Y → S σ-equivariant locally finite type of bounded dimension, the square formed by Psm and Rf_! from D^b_σ(Y;Λ) and D^b_σ(S;Λ) to Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) and Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 3.12
items.note: This is the paper's form of equivariant localisation; the proof uses the triangle j_!j^*F → F → i_*i^*F and the vanishing of Rf_!j_!j^*F in the Tate category by Corollary 3.11.

items.name: Tate cohomology of modules, complexes and sheaves
items.statement: For a Λ[σ]-module M, T^0(M) = M^σ/N·M and T^1(M) = ker(N)/(1-σ)M. For a bounded below complex C, T^i(C) = colim_n Hom_{D(Λ[σ])}(Λ, C[i+2n]) along the map Λ → Λ[2] induced by 0 → Λ → Λ[σ] →(1-σ) Λ[σ] → Λ → 0; it is 2-periodic in i, descends to D^b(Λ[σ]) and, for Λ = k, factors through the Tate category. For F ∈ D^b(S;Λ[σ]) with S carrying the trivial action, the Tate cohomology sheaves are T^i F = colim_n Hom-sheaf(Λ, F[i+2n]), and for Λ = k, T^i F ≅ Hom-sheaf_{Shv(S;T_k)}(k, T^* F[i]).
items.note: The module-level T^0, T^1 are Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group in degrees 0 and -1, which the libraries have; the complex-level and sheaf-level versions, with the colimit definition through the 2-periodicity map, are not.

items.name: Tate cohomology of a trivial action (Lemma 3.14)
items.statement: If C ∈ D^b(k[σ]) is inflated from D^b(k), i.e. σ acts trivially, then T^* C ≅ H^*(C) ⊗ T^*(k) with k carrying the trivial σ-action.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.14
items.note: This identity is what converts Tate cohomology of the shtuka stack for H back into ordinary cohomology, in equation (5.6) of the paper.

items.name: Relative Tate cohomology and the long exact sequence
items.statement: For F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k) and f: Y → S with S carrying the trivial σ-action, T^i Rf_! F is the relative Tate cohomology; when S is the spectrum of a separably closed field one writes T^i(Y;F). A distinguished triangle F' → F → F'' in D^b_σ(Y;k) gives a long exact sequence ··· → T^0 Rf_! F' → T^0 Rf_! F → T^0 Rf_! F'' → T^1 Rf_! F' → ···, 2-periodic.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.3; and §3.4.4
items.note: The long exact sequence of Tate cohomology of a finite group is in the libraries at the level of modules; the relative version for a morphism of schemes is not.

items.name: Equivariant localisation for Tate cohomology
items.statement: Proposition 3.12 specialises to: for F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k) and L the spectrum of a separably closed field with trivial σ-action, T^* RΓ_c(Y;F) ≅ RΓ_c(Y^σ; Psm(F)) in Shv(L;T_k). This encompasses the classical equivariant localisation theorems of Smith theory, for instance Quillen's Theorem 4.2.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.5; equation (3.11)
items.note: The statement that links this sheaf-theoretic formalism to classical Smith theory, and the form in which it is applied to shtukas.

items.name: JMW stratifications, parity complexes and parity sheaves
items.statement: Let Λ be a complete local PID and Y a stratified variety over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p whose stratification S = {Y_λ} is JMW: Ext^i(L,L') between finite Λ-free local systems on a stratum is Λ-free and vanishes for i odd. Fix a pariversity †: S → Z/2Z, here always the dimension pariversity. F ∈ D^b_S(Y;Λ) is even if for every λ the cohomology sheaves of i_λ^*F and i_λ^!F are Λ-free and supported in degrees ≡ †(Y_λ) mod 2, odd analogously, and a parity complex is a direct sum of an even and an odd complex. A parity sheaf is an indecomposable parity complex whose restriction to the dense stratum of its support is L[dim Y_λ]; if it exists it is unique and written E(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.1
items.note: Kac–Moody and in particular affine flag varieties over separably closed fields are JMW. Nothing in the atlas plans parity sheaves; EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves plans the perverse t-structure but parity is a different, mod 2 condition.

items.name: Structure of indecomposable parity complexes (Theorem 4.1)
items.statement: Let F be an indecomposable parity complex. Then its support is irreducible, hence of the form Y-bar_λ; i_λ^*F is a shifted Λ-free local system L[m]; and any indecomposable parity complex supported on Y-bar_λ extending L[m] is isomorphic to F.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.1
items.note: Juteau–Mautner–Williamson Theorem 2.12, the uniqueness statement that makes E(λ,L) well defined.

items.name: Tate-even, Tate-odd and Tate-parity complexes
items.statement: For F ∈ Perf_S(Y;T_O) with O = W(k) and a pariversity †: F is ?-Tate-even for ? ∈ {*,!} if T^{†(Y_λ)+1}(i_λ^? F) = 0 for every stratum, ?-Tate-odd if F[1] is ?-Tate-even, Tate-even (odd) if both * and !, and a Tate-parity complex if it is isomorphic in Perf_S(Y;T_O) to a direct sum of a Tate-even and a Tate-odd complex. A Tate-parity sheaf is an indecomposable Tate-parity complex whose restriction to the dense stratum of its support is T^*ε^*L[dim Y_λ] for an indecomposable O-free local system L; it is unique, written E_T(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.2; and Definition 4.4
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan's notion. Integral coefficients are essential: Ext^*_{Perf(T_O)}(T^*O, T^*O) = ⊕_i k[2i] is supported in even degrees, which is what the JMW condition needs.

items.name: Structure of indecomposable Tate-parity complexes (Proposition 4.3)
items.statement: Let F be an indecomposable Tate-parity complex. Then its support is Y-bar_λ for a unique stratum, and two indecomposable Tate-parity complexes with the same support and isomorphic restriction to the dense stratum of that support are isomorphic.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.3
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 5.5.6, proved by the argument of Juteau–Mautner–Williamson Theorem 2.12.

items.name: Modular reduction to the Tate category (Proposition 4.5)
items.statement: Let ε^*: D^b_c(Y;O) → D^b_c(Y;O[σ]) be inflation along the augmentation. (1) If F ∈ D^b_S(Y;O) is even (odd) then T^*ε^*F is Tate-even (Tate-odd). (2) If the parity sheaf E = E(λ,L) exists and Hom_{D^b_S(Y;O)}(E,E[n]) = 0 for all n < 0 — for instance if E is perverse — then E_T(λ,L) exists and T^*ε^*E(λ,L) ≅ E_T(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.5
items.note: The proof uses Hom_{Perf(Y;T_O)}(T^*ε^*F, T^*ε^*G) ≅ ⊕_{i∈Z} Hom_{D^b_S(Y;k)}(F F, F G[2i]). The slogan is: if all parity sheaves exist with vanishing negative self-Exts then T^*∘ε^* is a bijection from parity sheaves to Tate-parity sheaves.

items.name: Normalized parity sheaves and the lifting functor
items.statement: A normalized (Tate-)parity complex is a direct sum of (Tate-)parity sheaves with no shifts, giving Parity^0_S(Y;O), Parity^0_S(Y;k) and Parity^0_S(Y;T_O). Assuming all parity sheaves exist with vanishing negative self-Exts there is a lifting functor L: Parity^0_S(Y;T_O) → Parity^0_S(Y;k) sending E_T(λ,L) to E(λ,L⊗_O k) and, on morphisms, projecting to the i = 0 summand; it satisfies L ∘ T^*ε^* = F, the modular reduction.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.7; and the discussion of §4.4
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 5.6.6. The lifting functor is what converts the output of the Smith operation, which lives in a Tate category, back into honest sheaves with k-coefficients.

items.name: Parity sheaves on the affine Grassmannian are tilting modules (Theorem 4.8)
items.statement: If p is good for G then the Geometric Satake equivalence restricts to an equivalence Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Tilt_k(G-hat) between normalized parity sheaves for the stratification by L^+G-orbits and tilting modules for the dual group.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.8
items.note: Mautner–Riche Corollary 1.6, adapted from the complex affine Grassmannian to Gr_G over a separably closed field F. Goodness of p also gives that all parity sheaves exist and all normalized ones are perverse.

items.name: Tilting modules generate the derived category (Proposition 4.10)
items.statement: The natural projection K^b(Tilt_k(G-hat)) → D^b(Rep_k(G-hat)) from the bounded homotopy category of tilting modules is an equivalence.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.10
items.note: Riche Proposition 7.17, valid in any highest weight category. It is what lets a functor defined only on tilting modules determine the restriction functor on all representations.

items.name: The affine Grassmannian of H is the σ-fixed locus (Lemma 4.11)
items.statement: For G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation, the diagonal map induces an isomorphism Gr_H ≅ Gr_G^σ of subfunctors of Gr_G.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.11
items.note: The geometric input that makes the Smith operation available in the base change setting; it is the local counterpart of Lemma 5.7 for shtukas.

items.name: The norm functor Nm on the Satake category (Definition 4.12)
items.statement: For F ∈ Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;Λ), Nm(F) := F ⋆ {}^σF ⋆ ··· ⋆ {}^{σ^{p-1}}F, made σ-equivariant by the commutativity constraint of the convolution product; it is constructed first as a σ-equivariant perverse sheaf and then pushed through the realization functor into D_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;Λ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.12
items.note: The categorification of the p-fold convolution h * ··· * h appearing in the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh. Constructing the equivariant structure at the perverse level rather than the derived level is essential.

items.name: Stalks of Nm have filtrations by trivial and free modules (Lemma 4.14)
items.statement: Let i: Gr_H ≅ Gr_G^σ ↪ Gr_G and F ∈ Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) with O-free stalks and costalks of its cohomology sheaves. Then the stalks of the cohomology sheaves of i^*Nm(F) and the costalks of those of i^!Nm(F) each carry an O[σ]-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of trivial and free O[σ]-modules.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.14
items.note: The hypothesis (*) that makes Proposition 4.15 apply to Nm(F).

items.name: The Smith operation preserves parity (Proposition 4.15)
items.statement: Assume each stratum Y_λ is smooth and let E ∈ D^b_{S,σ}(Y;O) be a parity complex satisfying (*): all * and ! stalks of its cohomology sheaves at fixed points have an O[σ]-stable filtration with associated graded a direct sum of trivial or free O[σ]-modules. Then Psm(E) ∈ Perf_S(Z;T_O) is Tate-parity for the induced stratification Z_λ = Y_λ ∩ Z and the induced pariversity.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.15
items.note: A variant of Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 6.1.1. This is the technical heart of §4: it reconciles the Smith operation with a notion of t-structure-like constraint.

items.name: Base change of coefficients for equivariant parity sheaves (Lemma 4.16)
items.statement: If all strata Y_λ are simply connected and all parity sheaves E(λ,L) exist, then Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y;O) ⊗_O k → Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y;k) is an equivalence.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.16
items.note: Needed to descend the construction from integral to k-coefficients, and to make the categorical Frobenius twist of Construction 4.17 available.

items.name: Frobenius twist of a k-linear category (Construction 4.17)
items.statement: For a k-linear category C, C^{(p)} := C ⊗_{k,Frob} k has the same objects and Hom_{C^{(p)}}(x,y) = Hom_C(x,y) ⊗_{k,Frob} k; the tautological Frob-semilinear equivalence Frob_C: C → C^{(p)} is universal among Frob-semilinear functors out of C. A presentation C ≅ C_0 ⊗_{F_p} k induces a further k-linear equivalence C ≅ C^{(p)}, hence a Frob-semilinear self-equivalence Frob_{F_0} of C.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Construction 4.17
items.note: The categorification of the linearisation step in the normalized Brauer homomorphism; the algebra version is Construction 5.17.

items.name: The base change functor BC on the Satake category (Definition 4.18)
items.statement: BC^{(p)}: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) is the unique functor filling in the square whose top row is Psm ∘ Nm from Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) to Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O), whose left column is the modular reduction F and whose right column is the lifting functor L. Since BC^{(p)} is Frob-semilinear, one sets BC := BC^{(p)} ∘ Frob_p^{-1}, where Frob_p is the semilinear self-equivalence induced by the F_p-structure Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.18
items.note: The categorification of the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh §4.3, and the analogue of Leslie–Lonergan's functor LL describing the Frobenius contraction functor.

items.name: The base change functor is restriction along the diagonal (Theorem 4.20)
items.statement: Let Res_BC: Rep_k(G-hat) → Rep_k(H-hat) be restriction along the diagonal embedding H-hat → G-hat = H-hat^p, which preserves tilting modules. Then the square formed by BC on normalized parity sheaves, Res_BC on tilting modules and the two Geometric Satake equivalences of Theorem 4.8 commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.20; proved in Appendix A
items.note: The main theorem of §4 and of the appendix with Gus Lonergan: the base change functor realises Langlands functoriality on the geometric side. That Res_BC preserves tilting rests on the theorem that tensor products of tilting modules are tilting.

items.name: Exactness of the composite Psm ∘ Nm ∘ Sat (Lemma 4.21)
items.statement: The composite Rep_k(G-hat) →(Frob_p^{-1}) Rep_k(G-hat) →(Sat) Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) →(Nm) Perv_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;k) →(Psm) Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) is exact, i.e. sends exact sequences to exact sequences in the appropriate sense.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.21; proved in Appendix A §A.6
items.note: Exactness is what allows the functor, defined on tilting modules, to be extended to all of Rep_k(G-hat) through Proposition 4.10.

items.name: Galois equivariance of the base change functor (Lemma 4.22 and Corollary 4.23)
items.statement: BC: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F};k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_{H,F};k) is equivariant for the action of Aut(F/F_0); consequently, after equivariantization, the square formed by BC^{BAut(F/F_0)} on parity sheaves over F_0, Res_BC on Tilt_k(^LG^geom) and Tilt_k(^LH^geom), and the two Satake equivalences, commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.22; and Corollary 4.23
items.note: This is what makes the construction descend from the separably closed field to the ground field and hence apply to the geometric L-group, which is the form in which it enters Lafforgue's machine.

items.name: The integral compatibility cube (Lemma 4.24)
items.statement: The cube whose two horizontal faces are Psm from equivariant parity sheaves with O- and with k-coefficients, whose vertical arrows are the inclusions of parity categories into the constructible derived and Tate categories, whose diagonals are the modular reduction F and the lifting functor L, commutes; the unlabeled arrow on the top face is the one making that face commute.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.24
items.note: It says that the a priori mysterious top arrow has, after projecting to the Tate category, the simple description Psm; this is used when Tate cohomology is taken with coefficients in these parity sheaves.

items.name: Moduli stacks of shtukas with legs
items.statement: For X a smooth projective curve over F_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p and G a smooth generically reductive group scheme over X, Sht_{G,I} sends an F_ℓ-scheme S to the groupoid of tuples ((x_i)_{i∈I} ∈ X^I(S), an étale G-torsor E on X×S, and an isomorphism φ of E with its Frobenius twist away from the graphs of the legs). It is an ind-(locally finite type) Deligne–Mumford stack with a Schubert stratification, and π_I: Sht_{G,I} → X^I records the legs.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.1
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.2 plans multi-leg global shtukas as successive modifications with an isomorphism to the Frobenius pullback, with bounds, level, partial Frobenius and Harder–Narasimhan truncations, and the representability statements.

items.name: The Hecke stack and the Satake functor on shtukas
items.statement: Hk_{G,I} classifies two torsors with an isomorphism away from the legs; Geometric Satake gives Rep_k((^LG)^I) → D(Hk_{G,I};k), and pulling back along Sht_{G,I} → Hk_{G,I} gives Sat: Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) → D^b(Sht_{G,I};k), normalized as in Lafforgue. The Schubert stratification is the support stratification of the image of Sat.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.2; and §5.1.3
items.note: GS.1 plans global Hecke stacks and classical geometric Satake, and GS.2 the local-model maps to bounded Grassmannians defining the Schubert stratification.

items.name: Level structures, iterated shtukas and the partial Frobenius
items.statement: For D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, Sht_{G,D,I} → Sht_{G,I}|_{(X\D)^I} adds a trivialisation of E over D×S compatible with τ and φ. For a partition I = I_1 ⊔ ··· ⊔ I_r, the iterated stack Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r)}_{G,D,I} classifies a chain of torsors with modifications at the legs of each block and an isomorphism E_r ≅ {}^τE_0; the map ν to Sht_{G,D,I} is stratified small. The partial Frobenius F_{I_1} rotates the chain and applies τ to the legs indexed by I_1, lying over Frob_{I_1} on X^I.
items.note: GS.2 plans level, partial Frobenius and truncations; GS.4 plans the partial Frobenius action and Drinfeld's lemma with the verification that partial Frobenii commute with Hecke operators.

items.name: The base change setup for shtukas
items.statement: Let F be the function field of X, H_F reductive over F with a chosen parahoric extension H over X; let E/F be cyclic of degree p, corresponding to a smooth projective curve X', and set G := Res_{X'/X}(H_{X'}), a group scheme over X with generic fibre Res_{E/F}(H_E) and an action of ⟨σ⟩ = Aut(X'/X).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.7
items.note: The global setting of the paper; the σ-action on the whole shtuka tower is what Smith theory is applied to.

items.name: Admissible families of functors and the excursion action they carry
items.statement: A family H_I: Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Mod_A(Γ^I) over finite sets I is admissible if it is compatible with fusion, i.e. carries natural isomorphisms χ_ζ between H_I ∘ Res_ζ and Res_ζ ∘ H_J for every ζ: I → J, and with composition, χ_{ζζ'} = χ_ζ ∘ χ_{ζ'}. Given such a family, the composite H_{{0}}(1) → H_{{0}}(W^ζ) → H_I(W) →((γ_i)) H_I(W) → H_{{0}}(W^ζ) → H_{{0}}(1) defines the image of the generator S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)}, giving an A-linear action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H_{{0}}(1).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.1; and Construction 5.2
items.note: Feng's axiomatisation of Lafforgue's mechanism: this is the device by which an excursion action is constructed on any object built functorially out of the Satake category, and it is what he applies to Tate cohomology rather than cohomology.

items.name: Automorphic L-parameters after Lafforgue and Xue
items.statement: An L-parameter ρ ∈ H^1(Gal(F^s/F), G-hat(k)) arises from C_c^∞(Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ);k) if it arises through Proposition 2.4 from the Exc(Γ,^LG)-action on some irreducible Hecke subquotient, equivalently if the corresponding maximal ideal lies in the support of that space as an Exc(Γ,^LG)-module; ρ is automorphic if this holds for some D.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.5; with the discussion of §5.2.5
items.note: Lafforgue defined the action on the finite-dimensional cuspidal subspace; Xue extended it to all compactly supported functions, where no finite-dimensional subspace is stable, so the notion of arising has to be phrased through supports.

items.name: The partial Weil group acts through its quotient on Tate cohomology (Proposition 5.6)
items.statement: For any G, D, I and V, the FWeil(η^I, η^I-bar)-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) factors through the surjection FWeil(η^I,η^I-bar) ↠ Weil(η,η-bar)^I.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 5.6; proved in Appendix B
items.note: This is Drinfeld's lemma for Tate cohomology, and it is what makes the excursion formalism applicable to T^*(Sht_{G,D,I};V). GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma for the Hecke-finite sector of ordinary cohomology, not for Tate cohomology.

items.name: Tate cohomology of moduli of shtukas
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I)^σ-equivariant, the σ-equivariance of Sat and of π_I makes RΓ_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)) a σ-equivariant complex, and one sets T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) := T^j(RΓ_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V))), a module over T^0(H_G)[Weil(η,η-bar)^I] by Proposition 5.6. When σ acts trivially, Lemma 3.14 gives T^*(Sht_{H,D,I};F) ≅ H_c^*(Sht_{H,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};F) ⊗ T^*(k).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.3.1
items.note: Passing from cohomology to Tate cohomology is Feng's solution to the problem that the natural map between Sht_H and Sht_G is not Hecke-equivariant.

items.name: The shtuka stack for H is the σ-fixed locus (Lemma 5.7)
items.statement: If n is large enough that Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} and Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r),≤μ-tilde}_{G,D+nx_0,I} are representable by schemes, then the diagonal map H → G induces an isomorphism from the former onto the σ-fixed locus of the latter.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.7
items.note: The global analogue of Lemma 4.11 and the geometric input to equivariant localisation; the passage to representable truncations is what avoids Smith theory for stacks.

items.name: Cohomology and Tate cohomology at infinite level (Definitions 5.8 and 5.10)
items.statement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X. RΓ_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)) := colim_{n,μ} RΓ_c(Sht^{≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)), the colimit being over the covariant maps in μ and the contravariant pullback maps in n, a filtered colimit; and T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I};V) is its Tate cohomology. The indices for which the truncation is a scheme are cofinal.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.8; and Definition 5.10, with Remark 5.9
items.note: Necessary because the excursion action does not stabilise the pieces of cohomology cut out by bounding the Harder–Narasimhan polygon, so both n and μ must go to infinity.

items.name: Equivariant localisation identifies excursion operators (Theorem 5.11)
items.statement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X and a closed finite subscheme D. (i) For j ∈ {0,1}, under the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) ≅ H^j_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1) induced by Lemma 5.7, the action of S_{I,Nm^{(p^{-1})}(V),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(x),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(ξ),(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ is identified with the action of S_{I,Res_BC(V),x,ξ,(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LH). (ii) For j ∈ {0,1}, the action of S_{I, N·V, (N·x)∘Δ_p, ∇_p∘(N·ξ), (γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ on T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) is zero.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 5.11
items.note: The central global theorem: it converts the geometric identity BC = Res_BC of Theorem 4.20 into an identity between excursion operators for G and for H. Part (ii) is what makes the character extension of Lemma 5.15 applicable.

items.name: Equivariant localisation as an isomorphism of fusion-compatible functors (Proposition 5.12)
items.statement: Fix x_0 and D. (i) For j ∈ {0,1} there is a natural isomorphism of π_1(η^I,η-bar^I)-equivariant functors T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,I};Nm^{(p^{-1})}(V)) ≅ T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I};Res_BC(V)) on Rep_k(G-hat^I). (ii) For j ∈ {0,1} there is a natural isomorphism of functors Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Mod_k(Weil(η,η-bar)^I) with the same formula, compatible with fusion and composition.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 5.12
items.note: Compatibility with fusion and composition is exactly what Construction 5.2 needs, and is why the identity of excursion operators in Theorem 5.11 holds for all index sets simultaneously.

items.name: Global base change for automorphic parameters (Theorem 5.13)
items.statement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X and a closed finite subscheme D. If [ρ] ∈ H^1(Γ, H-hat(k)) is an L-parameter arising from the action of Exc(Γ,^LH) on H^0_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I};Sat(1))_α, then its image in H^1(Γ, G-hat(k)) arises in the action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H^0_c(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,I};Sat(1))_{φ(α)}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 5.13; which implies Theorem 1.6
items.note: The global main theorem. The index α records the connected component of Bun_G, matched by φ with that of Bun_H.

items.name: The Tate diagonal homomorphism (Definition 5.14)
items.statement: For A a commutative algebra in characteristic p with a σ-action, N·A is an ideal of A^σ and Nm: A → A^σ, a ↦ a·σ(a)···σ^{p-1}(a), is multiplicative but not additive; its composite with A^σ ↠ A^σ/N·A = T^0(A) is an algebra homomorphism Δ^p: A → T^0(A), the Tate diagonal.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.14
items.note: The algebraic mechanism behind the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh, isolated here as a general statement.

items.name: Unique extension of characters through the Tate diagonal (Lemma 5.15)
items.statement: Let A be a commutative F_p-algebra with a σ-action, κ a perfect field over F_p, and A' ⊂ A^σ a subring containing Nm(A) and N·A. Then any character χ: A' → κ factoring through A'/N·A extends uniquely to a character χ-tilde: A → κ, given by χ-tilde(a) = χ(Nm(a))^{1/p}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.15
items.note: The engine of every character-matching argument in the paper, both globally in Theorem 5.13 and locally in Theorems 6.21 and 6.26. It is the excursion-algebra analogue of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4.

items.name: Norm and norm-element formulas in the excursion algebra (Lemma 5.16)
items.statement: In Exc(Γ,^LG), Nm(S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)}) = S_{I,Nm(V),Nm(x),Nm(ξ),(γ_i)} and N·S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I, N·V, (N·x)∘Δ_p, ∇_p∘(N·ξ), (γ_i)}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.16
items.note: Identifies the multiplicative norm and the additive norm element of the σ-action on the excursion algebra in terms of its generators, so that the subalgebra of Definition 5.19 can be described explicitly.

items.name: Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras (Construction 5.17)
items.statement: For a k-algebra A, A^{(p)} := A ⊗_{k,Frob} k with the k-semilinear isomorphism a ↦ a ⊗ 1, universal among Frob-semilinear homomorphisms out of A. An F_p-structure φ_0: A ≅ A_0 ⊗_{F_p} k gives a k-linear isomorphism A ≅ A^{(p)} and hence a Frob-semilinear self-isomorphism Frob_{φ_0} of A which is the identity on A_0; precomposing a Frob-semilinear f: A → B with its inverse is the linearization of f. Exc(Γ,^LG) has such an F_p-structure because ^LG is defined over F_p.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Construction 5.17; with Example 5.18
items.note: The algebra counterpart of Construction 4.17, and the step that turns Br^p into a k-linear homomorphism.

items.name: The subalgebra Exc(Γ,^LG)' (Definition 5.19)
items.statement: Exc(Γ,^LG)' ⊂ Exc(Γ,^LG) is the k-subalgebra generated by N·Exc(Γ,^LG) and all elements Nm(S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)}) = S_{I,Nm(V),Nm(x),Nm(ξ),(γ_i)}; its local analogue Exc(W_v,^LG)' is Definition 6.22.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.19; and Definition 6.22
items.note: The subring A' of Lemma 5.15 in the case at hand: a character of it has a unique extension to the full excursion algebra, which is how the base change parameter is pinned down.

items.name: Hecke algebras, their centers and the Bernstein center in characteristic p
items.statement: For K ⊂ G_v an open compact subgroup of prime-to-p pro-order, H(G,K;Λ) := C_c(K\G_v/K;Λ) under convolution normalized so that 1_K is the unit, and Z(G,K;Λ) is its center; for K ⊂ K' convolution with 1_{K'} gives Z(G,K;Λ) → Z(G,K';Λ), and the Bernstein center is Z(G;Λ) := lim_K Z(G,K;Λ) over such K. It is the ring of endomorphisms of the identity functor on smooth k-representations of G_v, so every irreducible admissible Π gives a character χ_Π of Z(G).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.1
items.note: SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over rings with the normalized idempotents e_U defined exactly when the index denominators are units, and the corner description of U-biinvariant Hecke algebras; SR.3 plans the Bernstein center as natural endomorphisms of the identity, though in the complex case. The characteristic-p case is the one the paper needs.

items.name: The Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence
items.statement: For F_v a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p and G reductive over F_v, Genestier–Lafforgue construct Z_G: Exc(W_v,^LG) → Z(G); composing the character of Z(G) attached to an irreducible admissible Π with Z_G and applying Proposition 2.4 gives the semisimple L-parameter ρ_Π: W_v → ^LG(k). Writing Z_{G,r} for the composite with the projection to Z(G,K_r), K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}, the map is characterised by local-global compatibility.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.2; and §6.1.3
items.note: The semisimplified local Langlands correspondence over function fields, for all reductive groups and all irreducible representations. GS.7 plans a local–global comparison at a chosen place beginning from unramified Satake and GL_n, not this construction.

items.name: Local-global compatibility of the excursion action (Proposition 6.1)
items.statement: Let r ≥ 0 and D := rv + D^v with D^v supported away from v. For (γ_i)_{i∈I} ⊂ W_v^I, the excursion operator S_{I,f,(γ_i)} acts on H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) as convolution by Z_{G,r}(S_{I,f,(γ_i)}) ∈ Z(G,K_r).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 6.1; with Remark 6.2
items.note: Genestier–Lafforgue Proposition 1.3. For D^v large enough the action is faithful, so this characterises Z_G; the independence of the auxiliary global data is proved in their paper by a purely local construction with restricted shtukas, and is used here as a black box.

items.name: Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahorics and the Moy–Prasad filtration
items.statement: For H reductive over a local field F_v, B(H/F_v) is the Bruhat–Tits building; to x ∈ B(H/F_v) are attached the parahoric H(F_v)_{x,0} and its decreasing filtration H(F_v)_{x,r}, r ≥ 0, with H(F_v)_{x,0+} = ∪_{s>0} H(F_v)_{x,s} pro-ℓ. If E_v/F_v is unramified then H(E_v)_{x,r}^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r}, and if tamely ramified then the fixed points contain H(F_v)_{x,r}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.2.2
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans buildings with the group action and RG2.3 parahoric and congruence group schemes; the Moy–Prasad filtration in that generality and its Galois descent are the specific content used here.

items.name: The Cartan decomposition at a special vertex
items.statement: Let S be a maximal F_v-split torus of H, Z = Z_H(S), and Z := {z ∈ Z(F_v) : α(ω_Z(z)) ≥ 0 for all α ∈ Φ^+}. For a special vertex x in the apartment of S, H(F_v) = H(F_v)_{x,0}·Z·H(F_v)_{x,0}, and for z,z' ∈ Z the double cosets H(F_v)_{x,0} z H(F_v)_{x,0} and H(F_v)_{x,0} z' H(F_v)_{x,0} coincide if and only if z'z^{-1} ∈ Z(F_v)^0, the kernel of the Kottwitz homomorphism.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.2.2; quoted from Kaletha–Prasad Theorem 5.2.1
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4 plans the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their exact generality with the correct relative cocharacter lattice, dominance conditions and stabilizers.

items.name: Injectivity of the map of double coset spaces (Proposition 6.3)
items.statement: Let E_v/F_v be a finite Galois extension whose group has order coprime to ℓ, G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), x a special vertex in the apartment of a maximal F_v-split torus of G, K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^{Gal(E_v/F_v)}. Then for r ≥ 0 the map U_r\H_v/U_r → K_r\G_v/K_r is injective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 6.3
items.note: For r = 0 this is the Cartan decomposition; for r > 0 it uses that Gal(E_v/F_v) has order prime to ℓ while K_r is pro-ℓ, so that H^1(Gal(E_v/F_v); Stab_{K_r}(b)) vanishes. The referee suggested the simplification of the proof.

items.name: Surjectivity of restriction of Hecke algebras (Corollary 6.4)
items.statement: For r ≥ 0 the restriction map H(G,K_r;Λ)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} → H(H,U_r;Λ) is surjective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.4
items.note: The only consequence of §6.2 used later: it makes the Brauer homomorphism surjective and hence induces a map on centers.

items.name: Plain subgroups
items.statement: For K ⊂ G_v open compact with U := K^σ ⊂ H_v, K is a plain subgroup if (G_v/K)^σ = H_v/U.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.3.2
items.note: This is the σ-plainness condition of Treumann–Venkatesh §4.1, in the base change setting where the second condition of that definition is automatic. The same notion is routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16; the two routes must not both plan it.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism (Lemma 6.5)
items.statement: If K ⊂ G_v is plain, the restriction map from H(G,K)^σ = Fun_{G_v,c}((G_v/K)×(G_v/K),k)^σ to Fun_{H_v,c}((H_v/U)×(H_v/U),k) = H(H_v,U) is an algebra homomorphism, written Br.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.5
items.note: Introduced in Treumann–Venkatesh §4; the proof is that the terms of the convolution indexed by y ∉ H_v/U come in free σ-orbits, so contribute multiples of p. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.

items.name: Deep congruence subgroups are plain (Lemma 6.6)
items.statement: If K ⊂ G(F_v)_{x,0+} for some x ∈ B(G/F_v) then K is plain.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.6
items.note: Because G(F_v)_{x,0+} is pro-ℓ and σ has order p, all its subgroups have vanishing H^1(⟨σ⟩,-), so the fibre of H^1(σ,K) → H^1(σ,G_v) over the trivial class is trivial. This is what supplies plainness at every sufficiently deep Moy–Prasad level.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism computes the action on Tate cohomology (Lemma 6.7)
items.statement: Assume K ⊂ G_v is plain and Π is a σ-fixed representation of G_v. Then T^*(Π^K) → T^*(Π) lands in the U-invariants, and for every h ∈ H(G,K)^σ the square with vertical maps T^0h and Br(h) commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.7
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh §6.2. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, where it appears as the compatibility diagram (6.1).

items.name: The Treumann–Venkatesh homomorphism at level r (Definition 6.8)
items.statement: With K = K_r as in Corollary 6.4, Br: H(G,K_r)^σ → H(H,U_r) is a surjective algebra homomorphism, hence induces Z(Br) on centers, which factors through Z(H(G,K_r)^σ)/N·Z(G,K_r). Composing the Tate diagonal Δ^p: Z(G,K_r) → T^0(Z(G,K_r)) with Z(Br) gives a Frob-semilinear map, and Z_{TV,r}: Z(G,K_r) → Z(H,U_r) is its linearization with respect to the F_p-structure Z(G,K_r) ≅ Z(G,K_r;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.8; with Remark 6.9
items.note: Not in Treumann–Venkatesh, but inspired by their normalized Brauer homomorphism: this is the extension of that construction from spherical Hecke algebras to the centers of Hecke algebras at arbitrary Moy–Prasad level.

items.name: Compatibility of Z_{TV,r} with change of level (Lemma 6.10)
items.statement: For s > r the square formed by Z_{TV,s}, Z_{TV,r} and the maps e_G^{s→r}: Z(G,K_s) → Z(G,K_r) and e_H^{s→r}: Z(H,U_s) → Z(H,U_r) given by convolution with the appropriate indicator functions commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.10
items.note: The compatibility that lets the maps at each level be assembled into a map of Bernstein centers.

items.name: The base change homomorphism for Bernstein centers (Definition 6.11)
items.statement: Z_TV: Z(G) → Z(H) is the inverse limit over r of the Z_{TV,r}: Z(G,K_r) → Z(H,U_r). It is defined over any local field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p; its properties are proved here only for local function fields.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.11
items.note: This realises, in characteristic p, the base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers envisaged by Haines, for general groups and arbitrary depth.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism on permutation modules (Lemma 6.12)
items.statement: Assume K ⊂ G_v is plain. Then k[S-tilde^σ/U] is an H(G,K)^σ-direct summand of k[S^σ], and for all h ∈ H(G,K)^σ the action of h on k[S-tilde^σ/U] agrees with the action of Br(h) ∈ H(H,U).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.12
items.note: The function-level counterpart of Lemma 6.7, used to transport the excursion action through the identification of Tate cohomology of shtukas.

items.name: Tate cohomology of shtukas intertwines the two center actions (Corollary 6.13)
items.statement: For all r ≥ 1 the action of z ∈ T^0 Z(G,K_r) on T^0(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) agrees with the action of Z(Br)(z) on T^0(Sht_{H,D,∅};1) under the identification of the two Tate cohomologies coming from equivariant localisation.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.13
items.note: The bridge between the global identity of Theorem 5.11 and the purely local statement of Corollary 6.14.

items.name: Br identifies the local excursion operators (Corollary 6.14)
items.statement: For all r ≥ 1 and all data (V,x,ξ,(γ_i)_{i∈I}), Br carries Z_{G,r}(S_{I,Nm^{(p^{-1})}(V),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(x),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(ξ),(γ_i)}) ∈ Z(G,K_r) to Z_{H,r}(S_{I,Res_BC(V),x,ξ,(γ_i)}) ∈ Z(H,U_r).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.14
items.note: The key local consequence of the global equivariant localisation, obtained through Proposition 6.1 and the faithfulness of the action on the cohomology of shtukas for large auxiliary level.

items.name: Z_TV is compatible with φ_BC on excursion algebras (Corollary 6.15)
items.statement: The square formed by φ_BC^*: Exc(W_v,^LG) → Exc(W_v,^LH), Z_TV: Z(G) → Z(H) and the Genestier–Lafforgue maps Z_G and Z_H commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.15; which is the content of Theorem 1.4
items.note: The statement that the constructed base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers has the correct effect on Langlands parameters.

items.name: Unique σ-action on a σ-fixed representation (Lemma 6.16)
items.statement: If Π is an irreducible admissible σ-fixed representation of G_v, then the G_v-action on Π extends uniquely to an action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.16
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Proposition 6.1; it makes T^0(Π) and T^1(Π) well defined, with their H_v = G_v^σ-actions. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.

items.name: Linkage (Definition 6.17)
items.statement: An irreducible admissible representation π of H_v is linked with an irreducible admissible representation Π of G_v if the Frobenius twist π^{(p)} := π ⊗_{k,Frob} k appears in T^0(Π) or T^1(Π).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.17; with Example 6.19
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Definition 6.2. The motivating example G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic permutation gives T^0(π^{⊠p}) ≅ π^{(p)}, which is why the Frobenius twist is there. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.

items.name: The Treumann–Venkatesh conjecture (Conjecture 6.18)
items.statement: Conjecture: if π is linked to Π then π base changes to Π, i.e. ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Conjecture 6.18
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Conjecture 6.3, formulated here precisely using the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence, which did not exist when it was stated. Theorem 6.21 proves it in the form stated there. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, where it is the second conjecture of §6.3.

items.name: Tate cohomology realises base change, local form (Theorem 6.21)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let Π be an irreducible admissible representation of G_v and χ_{Π^{(p)}}: Exc(W_v,^LG) → k the character of its Frobenius twist. Form T^*(Π) as a smooth H_v-representation. Then for any irreducible character χ: Exc(W_v,^LH) → k appearing in the action on T^*(Π) through Z_H, the composite χ ∘ φ_BC^* agrees with χ_{Π^{(p)}}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.21; which implies Theorem 1.2
items.note: Proved by combining the compatibility (6.4) of Br with the action on T^*(Π), the identification of excursion operators of Corollary 6.14, the vanishing of Theorem 5.11(ii), and the uniqueness of character extensions of Lemma 5.15.

items.name: Base change of representations (Definition 6.23)
items.statement: For π irreducible admissible of H_v and Π of G_v over k, π base changes to Π if ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π in H^1(W_v, G-hat(k)). The fibres of the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence are used as a substitute for L-packets, which are not available for general groups and representations.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.23
items.note: The precise notion of local base change proved to exist in Theorem 6.26.

items.name: Hecke algebras are finite over their centers (Theorem 6.24)
items.statement: For every x ∈ B(G/F_v), every r ≥ 0 and K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}, the Hecke algebra H(G,K_r) with k-coefficients is finite over its center Z(G,K_r), which is itself a finitely generated k-algebra.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.24; with Remark 6.25
items.note: Quoted from Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss, who prove it over an arbitrary Z_p-algebra. The characteristic-zero statement is Bernstein's; the banal case was known to experts from Vignéras's work. This finiteness plus the Artin–Tate lemma and Nakayama is what produces the base change representation.

items.name: Existence of local base change with level control (Theorem 6.26)
items.statement: Suppose p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Fix x ∈ B(H/F_v), K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^σ. Let π be an irreducible representation of H_v over k with non-zero U_r-fixed vectors and L-parameter ρ_π. Then there is an irreducible representation Π of G_v over k with non-zero K_r-fixed vectors such that ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.26; which implies Theorem 1.1
items.note: The proof produces a maximal ideal m_π' of Exc(W_v,^LG)' whose unique extension is χ_π ∘ φ_BC^*, then uses the finiteness of Theorem 6.24 to find an irreducible H(G,K_r)-subquotient of H(G,K_r)/H(G,K_r)n_π on which the excursion algebra acts through it. Because x need not be a special vertex, Corollary 6.4 is not available and Br need not induce a map of centers.

items.name: Depth estimate for the base change (Remark 6.27)
items.statement: Let π be irreducible of depth r, with x ∈ B(H/F_v) such that π^{H(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0. If E_v/F_v is unramified, or tamely ramified, then B(H/F_v) = B(G/F_v)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} and (G(F_v)_{x,r+})^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r+}, so the proof of Theorem 6.26 produces a base change Π with Π^{G(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0 and hence depth(Π) ≤ depth(π); in the normalisation where H(E_v)_{x,pr} = G(F_v)_{x,r} the estimate reads depth(Π) ≤ p·depth(π).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Remark 6.27
items.note: The inequalities are expected to be optimal. The proof of the depth estimate uses neither Corollary 6.4 nor the Treumann–Venkatesh homomorphism.

items.name: Hyperbolic localisation and the constant term functor
items.statement: Fix a regular σ-equivariant cocharacter κ: G_m → H with centraliser a maximal torus T ⊂ G such that T_H := T ∩ H is maximal in H. The G_m-fixed points on Gr_G are the t^ν for ν ∈ X_*(T), with attracting semi-infinite orbits S_ν; CT_G := ⊕_ν Rp_{ν!} i_ν^* on monodromic complexes, and CT_G[deg_G] with deg_G(ν) = ⟨2ρ_G,ν⟩ is t-exact and is intertwined by Geometric Satake with restriction along T-hat → G-hat.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.4
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans semi-infinite geometry and constructibility, which is where hyperbolic localisation and the constant-term functor live; Remark A.1 notes that the displayed commutative diagram is not completely documented in the literature in this generality.

items.name: Compatibility of BC with the constant term functor (Lemma A.2)
items.statement: In the cube whose top face is Res_BC on Tilt_k(G-hat) and Tilt_k(H-hat), whose bottom face is Res_BC on Tilt_k(T-hat) and Tilt_k(T-hat_H), whose middle faces are BC on normalized parity sheaves for Gr_G, Gr_H, Gr_T and Gr_{T_H}, and whose vertical arrows are the restriction functors and CT_G[deg_G], CT_H[deg_H], the back, front, left and right faces commute.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma A.2
items.note: The reduction of Theorem 4.20 to the case of a torus: once the four side faces commute and CT is conservative, commutativity of the top follows from that of the bottom.

items.name: Conservativity of the constant term functor on the Tate category (Lemma A.3)
items.statement: The functor CT: Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) → Perf_{(L^+T_H)}(Gr_{T_H};T_k) is conservative.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma A.3
items.note: This is what makes the reduction to a torus legitimate in the Tate category.

items.name: Additivity of the base change functor
items.statement: BC(F ⊕ F') ≅ BC(F) ⊕ BC(F'): indeed Nm(F ⊕ F') ≅ Nm(F) ⊕ Nm(F') ⊕ (a direct sum of free σ-orbits), so the restrictions to the fixed locus differ by a perfect complex of O[σ]-modules and agree in the Tate category; the lifting functor L and Frob_p^{-1} are additive, and F is essentially surjective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.3
items.note: The first step of the proof of Theorem 4.20, and the reason the multiplicative norm Nm becomes additive after the Smith operation — the categorical shadow of the Tate diagonal.

items.name: Xue's Eichler–Shimura relation (Proposition B.1)
items.statement: Let v be a closed point of the open locus, of degree deg v. For any finite set I = I-tilde ⊔ {0} and any V ∈ Rep_k(G-hat^I) there is W ∈ Rep_k(G-hat) such that Σ_{α=0}^{dim W} (-1)^α S_{∧^{dim W - α}W, v}(F_{{0}}^{deg v})^α = 0 as an endomorphism of R^jπ_{I!} of the Satake sheaf restricted over v.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition B.1
items.note: Quoted from Xue Proposition 7.2.6. It is the input that lets Drinfeld's lemma be applied, by making the partial Frobenius act integrally over a finitely generated algebra.

items.name: The S = T theorem (Theorem B.2)
items.statement: S_{W,v} agrees with the Hecke operator T_{W,v} after restricting to (X \ (D ∪ v))^I.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem B.2
items.note: The identification of the excursion-type operator with the classical Hecke operator away from the point v, needed to run the Eichler–Shimura argument in Tate cohomology.

items.name: Eichler–Shimura in Tate cohomology (Lemma B.3)
items.statement: With v and I as in Proposition B.1, for any V ∈ Rep_k(G-hat^I) there is W ∈ Rep_k(G-hat) with Σ_{α=0}^{dim W}(-1)^α S_{∧^{dim W-α}W,v}(F_{{0}}^{deg v})^α = 0 as an endomorphism of T^j Rπ_{I!} of the Satake sheaf restricted over v.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.3
items.note: The Tate cohomology version of Proposition B.1, obtained from the long exact sequence for Tate cohomology.

items.name: The finite-type filtration on Tate cohomology (Lemma B.4)
items.statement: The submodule M^μ ⊂ T|_{η^I-bar} ≅ T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) is stable under the partial Frobenii F_{{i}} and of finite type over A^μ.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.4
items.note: Following Xue §1: the filtration by Harder–Narasimhan truncation is what supplies the finiteness hypothesis in Drinfeld's lemma.

items.name: Drinfeld's lemma applied to Tate cohomology (Lemma B.5)
items.statement: Drinfeld's lemma, in Xue's form (Lemma 7.4.2 of Xue), applied to the filtration of Lemma B.4 shows that the FWeil(η^I,η^I-bar)-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) factors through Weil(η,η-bar)^I, which is Proposition 5.6.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.5; concluding the proof of Proposition 5.6
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma in the lisse/finite-rank setting and its justification on the Hecke-finite sector, together with the continuous action of a product of global Galois groups; the application here is to Tate cohomology rather than cohomology.

items.name: Tate cohomology of a module over a cyclic group of order p
items.statement: For a Λ[σ]-module M with σ of order p, T^0(M) = M^σ/N·M and T^1(M) = ker(N: M → M)/(1-σ)·M, where N = 1 + σ + ··· + σ^{p-1}; these are 2-periodic in the index and a short exact sequence of σ-modules induces a six-term exact sequence.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4; the first display
items.note: Mathlib has the Tate complex and Tate cohomology of a finite group with the connecting map and the long exact sequence; Tau Ceti identifies degree 0 with M^G/NM and degree -1 with ker N/I_G M and proves 2-periodicity for a cyclic group, so T^0 and T^1 here are Tate cohomology in degrees 0 and -1 of ⟨σ⟩.

items.name: Witt vectors of an algebraic closure of F_p as coefficient ring
items.statement: O := W(k) is the ring of Witt vectors of the algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k; it is the integral coefficient ring for which the Tate category has Ext^* supported in even degrees and hence Tate-parity sheaves behave well.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.2
items.note: Mathlib has Witt vectors of a commutative ring of characteristic p with the ring structure, Frobenius, the Teichmüller lift and the discrete-valuation-ring statement for a perfect field.

items.name: The group ring of a cyclic group of order p and its flat modules
items.statement: Λ[σ] is the group ring of ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ over the p-adic coefficient ring Λ; for Λ = k a field of characteristic p it is Artinian local, so a module over it is flat if and only if it is free if and only if it is projective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.1; and §3.4.1
items.note: Mathlib has group algebras, their module theory, and the equivalence of flat, projective and free over an Artinian local ring; Feng's argument for Lemma 3.2 is exactly the chain of Stacks Project references for these facts.
